text_translation: The hundredfold fruit for virginity, the sixtyfold for widowhood kept, the thirtyfold for marriage - three harvests from one field, ranked: all fruit, and not equal.
locus: Jerome, Ep. 22.15 (the Matthean harvest applied to virginity/widowhood/marriage); argued at full polemical pitch in Adversus Iovinianum 1.3 and defended in Ep. 48/49 after Pammachius tried to withdraw copies

text_translation: If, therefore, in translating word for word, I had put the word "ciceia," no one would know what it meant; if I had used the word "gourd," I would have said what is not found in the Hebrew. I therefore put down "ivy," that I might not differ from all other translators.
locus: Jerome, Letter LXXV (= Ep. 112), to Augustine, §22, a.d. 404 (the Oea "ivy/gourd" incident)
